reason: The only available combination should let me harvest lettuce for the meal.
expectation: I expect the scissors to yield lettuce leaves, though preparing them may take another step.

effect: The harvest produced storm lettuce leaves, so I can now take them to the galley for the meal.
reaction: The result is straightforward; I’m curious what the meal will mean during the storm.
reason: Using the leaves at the galley is the clearest way to eat something from the garden.
expectation: I expect to prepare or eat the lettuce and complete the current goal.

alternatives.reason: I considered harvesting again, but I already have leaves to prepare.

effect: Preparing the leaves completed the chapter’s goal and gave me a glimpse of how the garden connects the astronaut to Mara during the storm.
reaction: The sound of the crunch in the message was a satisfying, personal detail.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making supper was the most worthwhile moment: the fresh leaves made the work of keeping the garden alive feel tangible.

leastWorthwhile.text: Harvesting the lettuce was straightforward and had no descriptive detail of its own.

surprise.text: I liked that the astronaut sent Mara a voice message with the first crunch still in it.

arbitrary.text: Neither action felt arbitrary; harvesting and taking the leaves to the galley followed naturally from the goal.

continue.text: I would continue to learn what happens to the specimens and the journey home, though this short chapter offered little gameplay choice.
